Subject: Medicore — packaging question: operator license vs site fee

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up with finance and our infra team this morning and two threads came up that I hoped you could clarify:

1) Operator license (per admin/operator seat) versus site fee (per site/GPU cluster) — which do you recommend for a multi-site hospital network like ours that expects spikey load and a mix of on-prem and cloud-connected sites?

2) How do you treat the platform fee for Private (VPC) — is that amortized monthly or billed up-front? And what are typical support tiers (response times, oncall) for a Tier 1 hospital deployment?

We also want to understand what concessions (if any) are available for a 3-year commit and whether migration/implementation credits are possible.

Appreciate a short write-up we can share with procurement.

Best,

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below, then attaching a draft term sheet and an XLS with scenario math. Happy to walk through live.

Short answers:
- Operator license (per-seat) favors smaller admin pools and gives simpler headcount-based billing; good when you want predictable OPEX tied to number of engineers/SREs.
- Site fee (per-site or per-cluster) favors fixed-capacity sites (edge sites with dedicated GPUs) and is better when you want predictable throughput budgeting across a hospital campus.
- Platform fee for Private/VPC is typically charged as an annual platform subscription; we can amortize it monthly for accounting if Medicore prefers.
- Support tiers: Standard (8x5 email, 24h response), Enhanced (10x5 + 4h P1), and Enterprise (24x7 oncall + 1h P1, dedicated CSM). For Tier 1 hospital we recommend Enhanced or Enterprise.

Tradeoffs and recommended construct for Medicore (short):
- Hybrid model: site fee for the high-throughput hospital campuses (ER/Imaging clusters) + operator licenses for central platform teams and dev/SRE. This minimizes per-token surprises while keeping admin count predictable.
- For spikes, include a burst pool (metered consumption) so you avoid huge overprovisioning.
- 3-year commit: we normally offer a graduated discount on platform fee and a one-time implementation credit (applied to SOW) in exchange for sizing/commit clarity.

I attached: Redwood_VPC_Termsheet_v1.pdf (showing both operator and site fee examples) and Medicore_MA_PlatformFee_Scenarios.xlsx with numbers under three load profiles.

If it helps, looping Marissa for commercial flex (discount ranges & credits).

— David

Samir — thanks for the questions. I ran the three scenarios and wanted to propose two commercial options we can put in a draft SOW:

Option A — Anchored site-fee primary (recommended for throughput predictability)
- Site fee covers N named clusters (per data center / hospital site). Operator licenses for central team (flat 25 seats).
- Platform fee: annual subscription, 10% discount for 3-yr commit.
- Implementation credit: $75k applied to SOW for signed 3-yr agreement, conditioned on staggered deployment milestones.
- Support: Enhanced (4h P1, 8x5 monitoring + annual on-site readiness workshop).

Option B — Operator-primary (recommended if Medicore prefers headcount OPEX)
- Operator licenses (per seat) for both central and local SREs. Add metered site BURST capacity that is charged per token for spikes.
- Platform fee: annual subscription, 5% discount for 3-yr commit.
- Implementation credit: $40k.
- Support: Enterprise (24x7 oncall) available at an uplift; first year discounted in Option B.

Notes / negotiation levers:
- We can convert a portion of the platform fee into implementation credits (effectively amortizing the platform fee into service dollars) if Medicore can commit to a minimal guaranteed monthly consumption.
- If you need escrow/airgap packaging for specific sites, that carries an additional per-site operator license but we can include a migration credit to offset initial uplift.

Samir — if you can share rough expected GPU/site counts and monthly token volumes for imaging and ER workflows, we’ll plug numbers into Option A and B and return final REDLINE-able term sheet.

Thanks — Marissa

Looping in a brief governance note from my side — approved commercial flex for enterprise health verticals:

1) For 3-year committed deals with >24 GPUs across sites we can offer up to 12% off platform fee (or equivalent implementation credit).
2) We will treat platform fee amortization as an accounting option but require a signed schedule that enumerates the amortization term.
3) On support tiers: we should default to Enhanced for initial rollout; Enterprise on steady-state sign-off if Medicore wants 24x7. Any on-site professional services beyond the readiness workshop should be scoped as SOW line items.

Marissa — you have authority to propose Option A with the $75k implementation credit for MDCR-4821. David — please propose a call this week to run through the numbers with Samir.
